article.body:
Hi there! We’re the Levin Family: Basya, Mimi, Chaim and

Yossi—chayolim just like you. Welcome to our podcast, where

Chayolim, in what way can this week’s lesson make a difference to you? What changes can you make in your own life?

But … don’t let it stop here! Conduct your own interviews at the Shabbos table. Choose someone

to be the podcast’s guest, and together explore how to live with the messages from the parsha.

Note: These images are for illustrative purposes only and are not meant to be an accurate depiction of the holy faces of the Tzaddikim.

Welcome Sara Imeinu to our Podcast for Parshas Chayei Sara!

Wow, the famous Parsha Podcast! Do you kids want to hear about your great-bubby’s special Shabbos licht?

Yes, please! I learned that Hashem made a miracle, and they stayed lit all week long. I wish mine would, too.

My dear, let me tell you some amazing things about your Shabbos licht that you might not have heard. Did you know that you light candles to bring shalom bayis into your home?

Yes! I learned in Gemara that the girls light candles so everyone can see. They keep us from tripping over things in the dark and getting hurt. The Shabbos licht keep us safe!

Yes. They do. They also help everyone in the house to do Torah and mitzvos.

Is it because if it was dark, then we wouldn’t be able to see the words in the siddur? Or learn? Or keep the food kosher?

But that was in the olden days. Nowadays, we just leave the lights on all Shabbos, so what’s the point?

Ah, well here is where you’re even more like your proud Imahos. You see, Shabbos licht bring gashmiyus and ruchniyus light. And b’ruchniyus, your candles also stay lit all week long! When you bentch licht on Erev Shabbos, you’re bringing powerful ruchniyus light into your home for the whole week. The lichtelach bring light into everything in the house, and they help everyone in the home to follow the teachings of Torah.

Whoa—even everything that I’m doing? And Tatty too?

Yes, everything! Every Jewish girl is called a “bas Sara, Rivka, Rochel, v’Leah,” so every Jewish girl has this special mission to light up the house, just like us!

When does it start working? Do we get this special mission at Bas Mitzvah?

Yes, but it’s important to practice. That’s why you started lighting your own candle as soon as you were able to understand what you were doing.

If I had such an important mission to light up the whole house for the whole week, I would also start practicing when I was three! It’s like the whole world is counting on the girls to do this!

Yes. Even more: the girls bentch licht before their mothers, so they are the first ones to bring the light into their homes.

Wow, so when I bentch licht, I better thank Hashem for giving me such a privilege!

Yeah, and practice for when I’m going to have my own house and children!

And when you do, you’ll teach your daughters to bring the light in the same way. Then, your licht will also bring a gashmiyus light to your home, and then to the whole world!
